page.title: Creative Agency vs Production Company for Community Organizations
page.description: Compare creative agencies and production companies for community organizations with checklists, decision criteria, and a side-by-side table.
page.h1: How do you decide between a creative agency and a production company for community organizations?
page.definition: A creative agency is a partner that develops brand strategy, messaging, and design systems, while a production company is a crew that executes live or recorded events, video, and streaming on the platform you choose.
page.quick_answer: Choose a creative agency when you need ongoing brand, content, and community strategy; choose a production company when you need a run of show, live crew, backup stream, and edited recordings for a specific event.

sections.h2: What does a creative agency deliver for community organizations?

blocks.p: A creative agency owns the long-term brand voice, content architecture, and community programming that turn rented reach into owned audience.

ul: Brand strategy and messaging framework
Design system and template library
Content calendar aligned to member journeys
Community programming and engagement playbooks
Owned audience growth: email subscribers and community members, not only followers

sections.h2: What does a production company deliver for community organizations?

blocks.p: A production company owns the technical execution of a single event or series, from run of show through backup stream and edited clips.

ul: Run of show and speaker brief with rehearsal
Branded slide template and lower thirds
Live producer, Q&A moderation, and platform operator
Backup stream ready on the real platform
Edited recording and highlight clips delivered within 24 to 48 hours

sections.h2: How do timelines differ between agency and production company?

blocks.p: Creative agencies work in ongoing cycles while production companies work in project windows tied to event dates.

head: Partner
Typical Window
rows: First plan runs 90 days; monthly review cycles
Webinar three to four weeks; summit or conference six to eight weeks

sections.h2: When should you hire each type of partner?

blocks.p: Match the partner to the problem: strategy and continuity versus execution and delivery.

ul: Hire a creative agency when you need a prioritized use-case list, tool choice, and roadmap for content operations
Hire a production company when you have a fixed agenda, platform selected, and need a show caller, speaker manager, and moderator
Keep in-house: strategy, brand voice approval, and product decisions
Outsource: moderation, member support, programming, onboarding, and reporting

sections.h2: How do costs compare for community events?

blocks.p: Production costs are published per event; agency fees are scoped per engagement.

ul: Moderated webinars: $2,500 to $7,500 per production
Executive summits, online conferences and hybrid productions: $10,000 to $50,000 and above
Creative agency work scoped per engagement; no fixed price published
West Peek Productions scopes content operations work per engagement; send the scope for a quote

sections.h2: What does West Peek Productions offer for community organizations?

blocks.p: West Peek Productions produces virtual, hybrid and webinar events and sets up marketing, content and creative operations.

ul: Event production on the platform you already use such as Zoom Webinars, Microsoft Teams, ON24 or StreamYard
Human-in-the-loop AI workflows for marketing, content and event teams
Community as a Service quoted by coverage hours, member volume, moderation risk, and programming
Creative operations setup with work management, asset management, and review tools

faq.q: Can a creative agency also handle live event production?
faq.a: Some agencies subcontract production crews, but the run of show, backup stream, and live crew are core production company deliverables. Verify who owns the technical rehearsal and platform operator role before signing.

faq.q: Do I need both partners for a community summit?
faq.a: If you lack an internal brand and content team, a creative agency builds the messaging and programming while a production company executes the live days. For repeat webinars, a production company alone may suffice.

faq.q: How do I evaluate a production company's backup stream capability?
faq.a: Ask for a recent run of show that includes a redundant encoder, secondary internet path, and a platform operator assigned to switch within seconds. Confirm they rehearse the failover during the technical check 60 minutes before going live.

faq.q: What tools should a creative agency bring for community content operations?
faq.a: Expect a work management tool such as Asana, Monday.com or Airtable; a brief repository in Google Docs or Notion; publishing via WordPress, Webflow or HubSpot; and reporting through GA4 and HubSpot.

faq.q: When should I involve a production company in the planning timeline?
faq.a: Lock the venue AV and platform before the agenda is final, ideally six to eight weeks out for a summit. Bring the producer in at intake so the run of show, speaker briefs, and rehearsal schedule align with the creative brief.
